svg.text: HARDWARE: A FRAME IS ITS BLOCK
The same colours in ENGINE and on the rack: a block's by its kind, its ports' by their group.
The frame's outline and band on the rack, the block's outline and cap in ENGINE. Hardware's kinds:
sound goes in to be heard: speakers, headphones, HDMI
sound comes out of it: a mic, a line in
GROUPS OF PORTS: A COLOUR A GROUP
The jack's ring on the rack; the port's dot and pill in ENGINE. A block's main group has the block's colour.
RYZEN HD AUDIO CONTROLLER · ITS SINK
One block, two groups: playback in, monitor out. Block and frame in the sink's teal; the monitor's ports violet.
RYZEN HD AUDIO CONTROLLER · ITS SOURCE
One block, one group: capture out. Blue, block and ports alike.
The same kind of block as the card's, so the same colours: hardware is hardware, by PCI, USB or Bluetooth.
A mono source: one meter column, no SPLIT, no BAL.
A Video/Source: ochre, its one port too. No meter, no SPLIT, no volume: PipeWire has none for video.
· On the rack, hardware's frames already look like this: a sink's frame teal, a source's blue, the monitor's jack violet. Nothing to change there.
· ENGINE changes to match: a block's colour by its kind (a sink teal, a source blue, a camera ochre), not one DEVICE blue for all of them;
and its ports by their group (playback teal, monitor violet, capture blue), not the block's colour.
· One table of colours, used by both: a block's colour is its main group's, so one block reads one colour from afar, its other groups close up.
· Next, the same for programs and PipeWire's own nodes: their kinds of block and their groups (INPUT, OUTPUT, MIDI…).
